---
title: "Filter and retrieve checklist records"
format: html
---

Here we present a practical guide to the `flora_records()` function of the `floraR` package. Unlike `flora_search()` and `flora_match()`, which resolve a list of names *you already have* against the checklist, `flora_records()` browses and filters the [Flora e Funga do Brasil (FFB)](https://floradobrasil.jbrj.gov.br/consulta/) checklist directly — no input name list required.

## Function Overview

`flora_records()` downloads and parses the FFB dataset automatically (like `flora_search()`, reusing the local cache on repeated calls), then applies whichever combination of taxonomic, geographic, and trait-based filters you request. All filters are combined with a logical AND, and the result always has one row per matching taxon.

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `taxon` | Character vector. One or more family, genus, or species names to filter by (e.g. `c("Fabaceae", "Luetzelburgia", "Inga edulis")`). |
| `taxonRank` | Character vector. Taxonomic rank(s) to keep (e.g. `"ESPECIE"`, `"VARIEDADE"`, `"SUBESPECIE"`). |
| `taxonomicStatus` | Character vector. FFB taxonomic status: `"NOME_ACEITO"` (accepted), `"SINONIMO"` (synonym), or `"NOME_DUVIDOSO"` (doubtful). |
| `state` | Character vector. Brazilian state(s), full name or acronym, diacritics-insensitive (e.g. `"Bahia"` or `"BA"`). |
| `phytogeographicDomain` | Character vector. Phytogeographic domain(s) (e.g. `"Caatinga"`, `"Mata Atlantica"`); accents are optional. |
| `endemism` | `TRUE` keeps endemics: all Brazilian endemics, or, combined with `state`, `phytogeographicDomain` or `vegetationType`, the endemics *exclusive* to those areas. `"Brazil"` keeps the Brazilian endemics occurring in the areas. `FALSE` keeps the complement of `TRUE`. See [Endemism](#endemism-brazil-or-exclusive-to-an-area) below. |
| `establishmentMeans` | Character vector. The origin of the taxon in Brazil: `"native"` (FFB's "Nativa") or `"introduced"` (FFB's "Exótica"); English or Portuguese, case- and accent-insensitive. |
| `lifeForm`, `habitat`, `vegetationType` | Character vectors. Life form (e.g. `"Arbusto"`), habitat (e.g. `"Terricola"`) and vegetation type (e.g. `"Cerrado (lato sensu)"`). |
| `version` | Character. FFB dataset version to use. Defaults to `"latest"`. |
| `rm_flora_database` | Logical. If `TRUE`, deletes the downloaded database after the search. Default `FALSE` keeps it cached for faster repeated queries. |
| `verbose` | Logical. If `TRUE` (default), prints progress messages. |
| `save` | Logical. If `TRUE`, writes the filtered records to a CSV file. |
| `dir`, `filename` | Where and under what name to save the CSV when `save = TRUE`. |

## Browse a whole family

```r
library(floraR)

fabaceae <- flora_records(taxon = "Fabaceae",
                          taxonomicStatus = "NOME_ACEITO")
```

## What each row contains

Every result has one row per taxon, with the taxon fields of the FFB checklist plus its distribution and species profile, the taxon's values joined in one cell with `" | "`:

```r
taxa <- flora_records(taxon = "Luetzelburgia",
                      taxonRank = "ESPECIE",
                      taxonomicStatus = "NOME_ACEITO")
```

| taxonName | state | phytogeographicDomain | endemism | lifeForm | vegetationType |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| *Luetzelburgia bahiensis* | BA \| PE \| PI | Caatinga | Endemica | Arbusto \| Árvore | Caatinga (stricto sensu) |
| *Luetzelburgia praecox* | GO \| MT \| TO | Cerrado | Endemica | Arbusto | Cerrado (lato sensu) |

The added columns are `state`, `phytogeographicDomain`, `endemism`, `establishmentMeans`, `lifeForm`, `habitat`, and `vegetationType`. They always describe the taxon's full FFB record: filtering by `state = "Bahia"` still shows every state a taxon occurs in. A field FFB does not record for a taxon is `NA`.

## Endemism: Brazil, or exclusive to an area

FFB records whether each taxon is endemic **to Brazil**. Asked for together with an area - `state`, `phytogeographicDomain`, or `vegetationType` - `endemism = TRUE` therefore means something stricter: the endemics **exclusive** to that area, whose whole FFB range lies within it.

```r
# All Brazilian endemics (22,252 accepted taxa)
brazil_endemics <- flora_records(endemism = TRUE,
                                 taxonomicStatus = "NOME_ACEITO")

# Endemic to Bahia: found only in Bahia (2,111 accepted taxa)
bahia_endemics <- flora_records(state = "Bahia",
                                endemism = TRUE,
                                taxonomicStatus = "NOME_ACEITO")

# Brazilian endemics that occur in Bahia, wherever else they also occur (6,655)
brazil_endemics_in_bahia <- flora_records(state = "Bahia",
                                          endemism = "Brazil",
                                          taxonomicStatus = "NOME_ACEITO")
```

The difference matters. *Luetzelburgia auriculata* is endemic to Brazil and occurs in Bahia - but also in 13 other states - so it is among the Brazilian endemics occurring in Bahia, not among the Bahia endemics. In *Luetzelburgia*, only *L. harleyi*, *L. neurocarpa*, and *L. purpurea* are endemic to Bahia.

Several values of one filter define one area, and several area filters must all hold:

```r
# Endemic to the region formed by Bahia, Pernambuco, and Piaui
ne_endemics <- flora_records(state = c("BA", "PE", "PI"), endemism = TRUE)

# Endemic to the Caatinga of Bahia: only in Bahia, and only in the Caatinga
bahia_caatinga_endemics <- flora_records(state = "Bahia",
                                         phytogeographicDomain = "Caatinga",
                                         endemism = TRUE)
```

`endemism = FALSE` returns the complement: without an area, the taxa not endemic to Brazil; with an area, the taxa occurring there that are not exclusive to it. A taxon with no FFB record for an area filter (e.g. no state-level distribution, as for some marine algae) cannot be shown to be exclusive to it, and is not counted as an endemic of it.

## Filter by origin

`establishmentMeans` - named after FFB's own field - is the origin of the taxon in Brazil. It keeps the taxa native to Brazil or those introduced into it, as recorded by FFB:

```r
# Introduced (exotic) species recorded in Bahia
bahia_introduced <- flora_records(state = "Bahia",
                                  establishmentMeans = "introduced",
                                  taxonomicStatus = "NOME_ACEITO")
```

English and Portuguese values both work: `"native"` or `"nativa"`, `"introduced"`, `"exotic"`, or `"exótica"`.

## Filter by phytogeographic domain and life form

```r
caatinga_shrubs <- flora_records(phytogeographicDomain = "Caatinga",
                                 lifeForm = "Arbusto")
```

## Save the result to a CSV file

```r
flora_records(taxon = "Luetzelburgia",
             save = TRUE,
             dir = "flora_records",
             filename = "luetzelburgia_records")
```

## Additional Tips

- `taxon` is matched against the `family`, `genus` and `taxonName` columns automatically — a family name ending in `"aceae"`, a single-word genus, or a multi-word species name are all detected and matched appropriately.
- Combine multiple filters freely: they are always ANDed together, so `flora_records(taxon = "Fabaceae", state = "Bahia", endemism = TRUE)` returns the Fabaceae species endemic to Bahia - found only there.
- Text filters (`phytogeographicDomain`, `vegetationType`, `lifeForm`, `habitat`, `establishmentMeans`) ignore case and accents: `"Mata Atlantica"` matches "Mata Atlântica", and `"Arvore"` matches "Árvore".
- If you already have your own species list to resolve rather than browse the checklist by criteria, use [`flora_search()` or `flora_match()`](/articles/resolve_species_names.qmd) instead.
